curated_dialogue_matrix.who_speaker: Dr. Benjamin Hudson, Ph.D. (Medievalist, Professor of History)
curated_dialogue_matrix.about_what: Etymology of surname 'Browder' as an Old English occupational contraction of 'browderer' (embroiderer/weaver), referenced in Wycliffe (1320-1384) and Chaucer (1343-1400).
curated_dialogue_matrix.key_quote: The name 'Browder' seems to be a contraction of the English word 'browderer'; this was an individual who carried out complicated sewing...

curated_dialogue_matrix.who_speaker: Vinnie King (Fellow Army Unit Member in Iraq)
curated_dialogue_matrix.about_what: Stated emphatically that Browders he knew in Ireland told him their family did NOT originate in Ireland/Scotland, but came from continental Europe (Netherlands).
curated_dialogue_matrix.key_quote: Both of these persons stated emphatically that... the Browders they knew told them that their families did NOT originate in either Ireland or Scotland... probably the Netherlands.

curated_dialogue_matrix.about_what: Believed and asserted that the Browder surname was of Flemish/Germanic occupational origin rather than indigenous Gaelic Irish.
curated_dialogue_matrix.key_quote: My great-uncle, Herman Edward Browder, who had done a great deal of research... clearly believed the Browder surname to have been of Germanic origin...

curated_dialogue_matrix.about_what: Recounted family traditions, Herman Browder's research papers, three emigrating brothers, and horses/tobacco planting in Virginia.
curated_dialogue_matrix.key_quote: I talked with extensively during my early days of family research... Herman Browder believed that the Browder family was of Germanic origin...

curated_dialogue_matrix.about_what: Gave sworn testimony confirming that Jesse Browder and Charles Browder (sons of William Browder Sr. & Margaret) died while serving in the Continental Army.
curated_dialogue_matrix.primary_source: Sworn Deposition of Peter Eppes, J.M. Browder Research
curated_dialogue_matrix.key_quote: Peter Eppes swore under oath that Jesse and Charles Browder, sons of William, died in Revolutionary War service...

curated_dialogue_matrix.medium: Personal Visit & Public Address at Guildhall
curated_dialogue_matrix.about_what: Exhorted and persuaded London citizens to advance a £200,000 loan to Parliament for military defenses.
curated_dialogue_matrix.primary_source: Gutenberg #20990 (London and the Kingdom Vol 3, p. 241)
curated_dialogue_matrix.key_quote: Earl of Manchester... paid a personal visit to the Guildhall and used their utmost powers to persuade the citizens...

curated_dialogue_matrix.who_speaker: Master of the Worshipful Company of Broderers
curated_dialogue_matrix.about_what: Sings 'The Master's Song' solo at 36 Gutter Lane hall, upholding brotherhood, embroidery craft, and faith under the motto 'Omnia desuper'.
curated_dialogue_matrix.primary_source: Worshipful Company of Broderers Official History
curated_dialogue_matrix.key_quote: The Broderers are the only Livery Company to have their own Master’s Song, which the Master has to sing solo...

curated_dialogue_matrix.about_what: Deposed regarding merchant suits involving Edmund Browder I, serge suits, French fall shoes, and land claims.
curated_dialogue_matrix.key_quote: Edmund Browder mentioned by name in early court records... regarding merchant account debts...
